plainTranslation:
This connection can keep both people on edge mentally.

One person may come into a conversation expecting it to go one way, and the other suddenly changes the direction. An idea gets interrupted. A plan gets challenged. A simple conversation becomes unpredictable. That can be exciting, but it can also become exhausting.

The attraction often comes from that same unpredictability. This person may crack your mind open. They may say the thing you did not expect, question what you thought was settled, or force you to think faster than usual. Boredom is unlikely here.

But the instability can become a pattern.

One person disrupts. The other tries to make sense of it. The disruption gets stronger. The attempt to make sense of it becomes sharper. Then both people feel misunderstood. One feels pinned down. The other feels like nothing can be settled.

Agreements can be hard to trust here. One person may genuinely change their mind from one conversation to the next. The other may start bracing for the next surprise. Over time, the mental excitement can turn into anxiety.

The real skill is knowing when the disruption is useful and when it is just chaos.

Some challenges open a new way forward. Others are only restlessness. When a conversation starts spinning, pause and ask what is actually being revealed. Is there a real insight here, or are you just knocking the table over because sitting still feels uncomfortable?

This aspect works best with a few anchors that do not move. Certain plans, promises, and routines need to stay reliable. Not everything can be up for debate all the time.

The friction is about style, not worth. Needing things to make sense is not small-minded. Needing mental freedom is not a rejection. Both can be true.
